A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research lineage despite the changed title and broader matroid framing in v2. Their complete main texts, equations, figures and appendices are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports mathematical proofs, constructed examples and analytical bound plots. Neither its main text nor Appendices A–C reports original experiments, simulations or data analyses.

after.justification: v2 remains theoretical throughout, including Appendices A–B. Its random-coloring and random-graph results are proved analytically; its plots illustrate mathematical bounds rather than empirical outcomes.

M1.justification: The core opportunity-fair optimization is retained. v2 Section 2.2 adds an explicit coordinatewise rounding-down conversion from fractional allocations to feasible integral allocations with approximate fairness, providing a limited additional output procedure.

E1.justification: Neither version uses datasets or performs empirical task evaluations. The additional matroid classes and random-coloring scenarios extend the theoretical setting, rather than evaluated dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: Neither version empirically evaluates comparison methods. Shapley, leximin and other fairness notions are mathematical alternatives, and related-work citations do not constitute evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Neither version reports experimental evaluation protocols. Revised random-graph probability regimes are assumptions of theoretical results, rather than changes to experimental settings.

E4.justification: Neither version contains empirical ablations, robustness tests or error analyses. The added structured and stochastic analyses consist of theorems, proofs and mathematical constructions.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental run counts, uncertainty estimates or significance tests. Concentration inequalities and high-probability statements belong to the theoretical proofs.

E6.justification: Neither version contains empirical result entries. v1 Figure 10 survives as v2 Figure 9 with the same analytical bound; newly plotted bounds and revised mathematical findings are covered under T1.

T1.justification: v2 generalizes the polymatroid characterization and retained worst-case and parametric bounds to colored matroids. It adds rounding guarantees, random-coloring results, graphic random-graph bounds and demographic-parity convergence (Sections 2.2 and 4.3–4.4; Appendix B.3), while removing v1's detailed leximin norm/projection and weighted-projection results. The dense bipartite threshold changes from log-squared(n)/n to omega log(n)/n. The new Theorem 4.7 also contains inconsistencies between its stated formula and Appendix A.4.

C1.justification: The abstract and contributions shift from fairness in bipartite matching to opportunity fairness across matroid allocation problems. v2 makes the new semi-random claim that no dominant group implies asymptotically no welfare loss central to the paper. The earlier worst-case group-count bound remains, with broader applicability.

C2.justification: v2 interprets semi-random welfare loss through group dominance and explains why arbitrarily small groups can coexist with no asymptotic loss. It quantifies the fractional-allocation approximation and replaces v1's discussion of weighted edges and two-sided matching with questions about intermediate matroid families, unresolved random-graph density regimes and concave welfare objectives.

D1.justification: Computational documentation is substantially reduced. v1 provides serial-dictatorship and probabilistic-serial pseudocode plus explicit matching-variable LPs and tight-constraint recovery in Appendix B. v2 omits these constructions and instead states separation-oracle computability conditions. Appendix A.4 newly identifies Mathematica's Reduce function for symbolic verification.

R1.justification: Related work is substantially reframed around fair matroid and submodular allocation, Kalai-Smorodinsky fairness and beyond-worst-case analysis. Additions include El Halabi et al. (2020, 2024), Kalai and Smorodinsky (1975), Nicosia et al. (2017) and Roughgarden (2020). v1's detailed positioning against fair division with matroid-rank valuations is curtailed.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and main narrative are extensively rewritten around opportunity fairness and matroids. The geometric and fairness discussions are consolidated, retained alternative fairness notions move to Appendix B, and the appendices are reorganized around the expanded theory.

P2.justification: The visual presentation is substantially revised: feasible-set and fairness diagrams are redrawn in color, algorithm panels disappear, and graphic-matroid constructions and numerous proof-transformation diagrams are added. v1 Figure 6 becomes v2 Figure 20, while the retained bound plot moves from Figure 10 to Figure 9; v2 Figure 10 presents the new random-coloring bound.

improvement.justification: The broader matroid treatment and new random-coloring analysis offer substantial gains in scope and explanation. However, the central new Theorem 4.7 uses a denominator C where Lemma A.6 derives lambda. Its unqualified relaxed bound C - 1/pi also equals zero at the balanced distribution pi = 1/C, contradicting PoF being at least one. These unresolved inconsistencies weaken confidence in the principal addition, preventing a reliable net quality judgment.
